subject: Private VPC commercial proposal and support-tier tradeoffs
messages:
From: Rachel Park <rachel.park@acme.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.ai
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Intro: final commercial asks for VPC/private deployment

Markus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here at Acme is consolidating final commercial terms for our Private VPC rollout. We need: 

- A clean SKU breakdown for the on‑prem / VPC license (per-node vs. per-seat options)
- Platform fee treatment (annual amortization vs upfront) and whether it can be capitalized
- Supported support tiers, oncall SLAs, and related pricing (standard, premium, enterprise)
- Any available migration/implementation credits and typical SOW language for engineer time
- A proposal showing tiered discounts vs commit (12/18/24 month) and an example annual price for our expected footprint (~12 GPU nodes peak, largely steady)

Our timeline: Procurement aims to issue the PO by 12/31; legal will want a draft SOW + MSA addendum to review. If you can share a short workbook with figures and an annotated SOW, that would speed things up.

We are also seeing internal sensitivity around the platform fee line item — is there flexibility to amortize or reduce it for a reserved capacity deal?

Appreciate a concise proposal and next steps.

Thanks,
Rachel
Head of Procurement, Acme AI
procurement@acme.ai

---
Attachments referenced: none in this message.
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Rachel Park <rachel.park@acme.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro: final commercial asks for VPC/private deployment

Rachel —

Appreciate the clear list. I've pulled together a short workbook that lays out: SKU options (node vs seat), platform fee amortization examples, three support tiers and their SLAs, and discount bands for 12/18/24 month commits. See attached: acme_vpc_pricing_workbook.xlsx and draft_contract_terms.docx.

High level summary up front to unblock procurement:
- Licensing: two recommended paths: (A) node-based bundle for predictable throughput (recommended for steady workloads) or (B) seat-based license if you prefer user-level accounting. Workbook lists both with example math for 12 nodes.
- Platform fee: we can amortize the platform fee monthly over the committed term; standard policy is upfront but we support annual prepay with an equivalent discount.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours, 24h ticket triage), Premium (24/7 oncall with 4h response for sev1), Enterprise (named TPM, monthly ops review, 1:1 runbook onboarding).
- Migration credits: we typically offer implementation credit against the first invoice for committed deals (amount varies vs commit).
- Discount bands (example): 8% at 12mo, 12% at 18mo, 17% at 24mo on license line items. Platform fee normally excluded from deep discounting but can be partially reduced based on total ARR.

Two asks to help tighten the proposal: 1) confirm whether Acme prefers node vs seat accounting, and 2) confirm whether procurement needs prepay (invoice upfront) or prefers monthly billing.

I can hop on a quick call with procurement/legal today if helpful — happy to walk the workbook.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

Attachments: acme_vpc_pricing_workbook.xlsx, draft_contract_terms.docx
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro: final commercial asks for VPC/private deployment

Markus — quick internal notes before we reply to Acme: 

1) Discount posture: given Acme's size and 12 GPU baseline, we can be more aggressive on license discount if they commit to reserved capacity (node bundle) and 12+ month prepay. Suggest starting with 12% at 12mo prepay, 15% at 18mo prepay, 18% at 24mo prepay for license lines. Platform fee: propose a capped reduction (25% off) if they take 24mo prepay.

2) Support: push them to Premium for mission critical (we include migration credits tied to Premium). Premium is easier to sell because it bundles higher onboarding hours.

3) Legal: our draft_contract_terms.docx will need the MSA addendum for onprem data handling and an explicit IP clause re model artifacts. Share discount_playbook.pdf for reference on approval thresholds — anything above 15% needs signoff by SVP GTM (Sean).

Next step: Markus, if you can present a two‑option offer to Acme (Conservative: 12mo, 12% + Premium; Accelerated: 18mo, 15% + Premium + migration credits), we can likely close before 12/31.

- Vanessa
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: discount_playbook.pdf
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 11:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro: final commercial asks for VPC/private deployment

Thanks team — a couple of practical counterpoints: 

- Migration credit sizing: recommend a fixed 40 engineering hours credit (applied against SOW) for the Accelerated offer; that lands as an operational concession without us carving too much off price.
- Platform fee amortization: confirm whether Acme's accounting wants capitalization. We can provide a billing memo to support capitalization, but can't change the invoice timing beyond prepay vs monthly.
- Risk protection: include a 3‑month rollback clause in the SOW (customer can return to hosted for minimal penalty) — this reduces legal friction.

If Acme agrees to 18mo + Premium + credit, we can authorize 15% discount on license lines and 20% off the first quarter of platform fee as a one‑time onboarding concession. Anything deeper (>=18% license discount or >25% platform fee reduction) requires Sean's signoff.

Grace O'Connor
Head, Customer Success & Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Rachel Park <rachel.park@acme.ai>, Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Intro: final commercial asks for VPC/private deployment

Rachel —

Thanks for the patience. Based on our internal alignment, here are two simple buy boxes that match your asks and should be ready for procurement/legal review: 

Option A — Conservative (fastest to PO)
- Term: 12 months, prepay annual invoice
- Licensing: node-based bundle for 12 nodes
- Discount: 12% on license lines
- Platform fee: amortized monthly; no additional reduction beyond standard policy
- Support: Premium (24/7 oncall, 4h sev1)
- Migration credit: 20 engineering hours applied to first SOW
- Next steps: we can share a draft SOW and MSA addendum today; target PO by 12/31.

Option B — Accelerated (best economic)
- Term: 18 months, prepay annual invoice (invoiced annually)
- Licensing: node-based bundle for 12 nodes
- Discount: 15% on license lines (requires internal approval completed)
- Platform fee: 20% off the first quarter as onboarding concession; amortize remainder over term
- Support: Premium + named onboarding (ops runbook)
- Migration credit: 40 engineering hours applied to SOW
- Legal: include 3‑month rollback clause in SOW to address runbook/rollback risk

Attachments: acme_vpc_pricing_workbook.xlsx, proposed_sow_vpc.pdf, draft_contract_terms.docx
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2345
DocuSign (template): https://docusign.com/templates/rdw-acme-vpc

If Option B is acceptable, we have internal approval to proceed at the 15% license discount level and the onboarding concessions listed. Anything materially different will require Sean's final signoff. Please confirm which option you prefer and whether procurement needs the SOW in Word or PDF — we can deliver both.

Happy to jump on a short call tomorrow to run through the SOW with legal.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Private Deployments
